changes.text: New: live queue reports. Join a playable game's line with one tap, add a rough count of people ahead, and close it when you get in or leave.
Waits reported by other visitors now sit beside the guide's forecast, with how many people reported and how long ago.
Queue timing keeps working without reception — a wait you finish offline is sent once you are back online.
No account needed to report: no names, no locations, and reports are only kept for the show.
Reporting has its own Live queues tab, so cards carry a single “Report a queue” link instead of buttons under every game. It appears while the show is on.
Queue details are saved by the “Done” button now — picking a queue type and walking away used to discard it.
You can only track one queue at a time. Joining a new line asks whether to leave the one you are in, and records that you left it.
New: share a single booth. The Share row on a card hands out a link, with a QR code under it, that opens the guide on that card rather than at the top of the list.
A card turned to its business booth shares that booth, and a link to one switches the trade exhibitors on so it has something to open.
The corner of a card is three rows now — Save, Played, Share — each with a word on it, at a fixed width, so pressing one no longer moves the exhibitor's name.
An exhibitor's name stays inside its own card on a small phone. Long names used to run out underneath the buttons, especially in German.
A booth's details can be closed on a phone held sideways — the card used to slide under the hall chips, taking its × with it.
Held sideways, those details open as a panel down the right-hand edge, so the hall stays on screen beside them.
The hall map keeps more of a sideways screen for the hall itself, and stays clear of the notch.
The plan's day chips are one line again on a phone: they scroll sideways instead of wrapping onto a second row.
The business-hall banner goes away once you have switched the trade exhibitors on. The hall chips still mark those halls trade-only.
The credit line under the map is shorter, so it costs fewer rows on a phone.
Google Play's Hall 7 lineup confirmed playable: Fruit Ninja, Dave the Diver, Subway Surfers City, eFootball, Wobbly Life and Asphalt Legends Unite.
LEGO Skylines added as a rumored title for LEGO's Hall 9.1 booth, based on a leaked ratings-board filing.
MBC Game Studio's business-hall booth added: Hall 2.1, A057, alongside its Hall 8.1 showcase.
Sorting, filtering and searching the exhibitor grid is about three times quicker, and the search box keeps up with typing now.
Saving a booth, or opening the trade list or the full directory, happens on the tap rather than after a pause.
Taps land while the guide is still starting up, and the exhibitor grid arrives a screenful at a time.
Switching tabs is about twice as quick.
Today no longer misses your business-hall stops while the trade directory is still loading — it fills them in as soon as it lands.
A day made entirely of business-hall booths opens on Today, the way any other day does.
Ticking off the last stop of the day keeps the keyboard's focus ring on screen.
Today cannot outlive the show: a phone left open on it past Sunday moves to the Visit planner.
New: a Today tab, during the show only (Aug 26–30). Your stops for the day in hall order, with the ones you have ticked off folded away.
Its top is a clock: today's access and hours, whether the halls are open now, how much of the day you have got through, and which stop has the worst queue.
It reads your existing plan, so only stops you gave a day appear. The rest are counted underneath, with a way through to the planner.
During the show the guide opens on Today whenever the day has something on it.
The plan stops moving under you. Assigning a day, ticking a stop off or nudging one with ▲▼ used to throw the page down the board; it stays where you left it now.
Keyboard and screen-reader users keep their place: focus still lands on the button you pressed, and the page follows only when the stop really moved.
The plan board, the queue table and the full directory no longer shift what is under them while they update.
On a phone held upright the hall map now opens on its side, filling the screen, with booth names about half again as large. Turn the phone and it turns back.
Halls 10.1 and 10.2 stay as they are, and nothing turns on a wide screen. The button under the zoom controls turns the hall by hand.
Everything on a turned hall stays the right way up — names, doors, saved stands, numbered pins — and a link to a booth opens the same stand.
Korea Pavilion (KOCCA) booth corrected: Hall 3.2, C050g/D051g, not Hall 2.2. Confirmed against the official directory and two press reports.
Google Play's Hall 7.1 booth detailed: a Fruit Ninja live arena plus demo stations for Dave the Diver, Subway Surfers City, eFootball, Wobbly Life and Asphalt Legends Unite.
Directory refresh: 1,751 registered exhibitors (up from 1,723).
22 new exhibitors from the directory sweep. Hall 10.1's hardware row: Gateron, DeepCool, Lexar, XPPen, EPOMAKER, IQUNIX, Genki, HAVIT, KARNOX, Diablo Chairs, iiyama, Game Informer.
Hall 5's Cards & Boards area: Ravensburger, Panini, Bushiroad, Pegasus Spiele, PureArts, Tsume Art, Fangamer.
Hall 10.2: Retro Games Ltd, Shueisha Games, Metanet Software.
Gamescom's show floor has sold out to exhibitors for the first time — 233,000 m², 1,600+ exhibitors. Folded into the crowd guidance on the Info tab.
The Share button and the footer links are easier to hit: same size and place, bigger tap area around them.
A booth with several stands in one hall wears one number on the map, not one per stand — Nintendo's four Hall 9 stands drew four pins reading “2”.
The hall chips count stops now rather than saved stands, so their numbers match your plan whether or not a day is picked.
Each day's heading in By day carries a “Map →” that opens the site overview with that day already picked, the way By hall's headings do.
Headings the planner jumps to no longer land underneath the masthead.
The tab row says that it scrolls: a ▸ plate sits at whichever edge still has tabs past it, so Updates is no longer hidden off the right of a phone.
The hall plates in Event info's Halls & areas list are easier to hit — the number keeps its size, the tap area around it grows.
The count under the hall map agrees with the chip above it: “5 saved” counts stops now, like the rest of the guide, not lit rectangles.

The hall map's day route no longer stops at the wall. With a day picked, the hall says which halls come before and after it, as buttons, and the route line runs out to the doorway that starts the way there.
The arrow marks the opening nearest the stop you are leaving and names the hall it leads to. Seven of the thirteen halls have no doorways recorded yet, so they name the leg without drawing it.
A hall with nothing planned in it still gets both legs, so walking through it tells you which way is which.
The campus overview answers the same question one step back: with a day picked, every hall it touches is lit and numbered in order, and the counts switch to that day's stops.
None of this is a walking route — the numbers are your plan's own order, and the line just joins them.
Your plan is yours to order: ▲▼ buttons move a stop up or down its day or hall, and the order sticks, pins on the hall map included. “Reset order” hands it back to busiest-queue-first.
Moving a stop only moves it inside the day or hall you are looking at, and a booth saved later joins at the end of its group.
By day now shows each stop's queue index — Q5 · Extreme, Q2 · Light — the way By hall always has. Business-hall booths say “Trade badge” instead.
The order travels with your plan, so a second window and the hall map pick it up too.
New on the hall map: your plan, drawn on the floor. Pick a day in the Plan row and that day's stops get numbered pins, in the order your plan board lists them.
The line joining the pins is the order, not a walking route — nobody publishes where the aisles run.
The “Map →” links in By hall carry a single-day filter across now, so the hall opens with the route already drawn.
A booth with two stands in the same hall wears its number on both, and tapping a numbered stand says “Stop 2 of 5”.
Amazon Web Services' business booth was filed at a stand the hall plan gives to nobody. Corrected to A051 next door, per the directory and the hall plan.
Four dead official-profile links removed: Nintendo, Tencent — Worlds of Play, Eclipse Glow Games and MBC Game Studio. Only the outbound link is gone.
Directory refresh: 1,723 registered exhibitors (up from 1,711).
Re-checked LEGO, Bilibili and Google Play's lineups, EA's slate beyond FC 27 and Xbox's unannounced slots — still no specifics.

The hall map has an overview now, the first chip in its hall row: the whole site at once — halls, the Boulevard, the passages and the four gates, with your saved count on each. Tap a hall to open its plan.
Halls 1 and 11 are on it too, greyed out. The guide covers no booths in either, but they keep the halls around them in the right place.
The map opens on the whole site if you ask it to: the hall row's first chip is a campus overview, with your saved-booth count on every hall it draws. Not to scale.
Zoom buttons on the map beside the gestures: in, out, and one that fits the whole hall back on screen. A stand's sheet also says which day you planned it for.
The map's ← goes back where you came from now, and the address bar names the hall on screen, so the link you copy is the place you are looking at.
Hall 5.1 is on the map: Cosplay Village, the Artist Area and the ground-floor merchandise shops, drawn booth by booth — 141 stands. Both rows in Halls & areas open it now.
Hall plans re-snapshotted: CD Projekt's Halls 8.1 and 4.2 booths are now filed as CD PROJEKT RED, and Bonfire Studios joins Gamer Network's Hall 2.2 stand.
Fixed on the map: saved-booth counts on the hall chips and overview plates could read low, and with a trade badge on, the business halls' counts were missing altogether.
The Visit planner gets a jump nav under its lede — it runs five screens deep on a phone, and most people come back for their plan or the queue table.
The five-days board now wears each day's plan count — “2 stops in your plan” — and tapping one goes straight to those stops.
The plan's day headers no longer repeat that day's whole advice paragraph. Day, access, hours and the business-area warning stay.
Ubisoft's Community Lounge gains Assassin's Creed Shadows in its developer-talk schedule — still one playable demo, Rayman Legends Retold.
Directory refresh: 1,711 registered exhibitors (up from 1,659).
Re-checked Google Play, LEGO, Bilibili and EA's lineups and Xbox's unannounced slots — still no specifics. An insider now claims Xbox has a new IP planned for Opening Night Live; unconfirmed.
Fixed, and it was the bad kind: day assignments could vanish on reload, and the next change wrote that loss back for good. They survive now.
Halls & areas on the Info tab opens the map now. Each row's hall plate is a link, and a row naming a span — “5–10”, “2–4” — lands in the first hall of it.
The map names a hall's doors from the widest zoom — “Boulevard”, “Hall 6.1”, “Hall 11” — rather than one zoom band in.
Korea Pavilion (KOCCA) booth confirmed: Hall 2.2, C050g/D052g. One consolidated business-hall stand for 13 Korean studios this year, so it takes a trade badge.
Fixed: Logitech G was pointing at the wrong stand. It holds its own Hall 10.1 stand at E074/F077.
Added AULA to Hall 10.1's hardware row (mice, keyboards; booth E050), filed under Shenzhen Suoai Electronics Technology.
Fixed two business-hall booths: AWS's Hall 3.2 stand (now B040g/C041g) and IGDA's second, adjacent one (C014/D015 added).
Re-checked Google Play, LEGO and Bilibili's lineups, EA's slate beyond FC 27 and Xbox's unannounced slots — still no specifics.
Directory refresh: 1,659 registered exhibitors.

Coverage pass over the entertainment halls — thirteen booths that showed as uncovered now have cards. Hall 6.1: 4Divinity (A030), Secret Mode (B040), Pawprint Interactive (C041), Elementa Games (C021).
Hall 7.1: 4Divinity's main stand (B021/C020), Huawei's AppGallery (B031) and Webedia's FYNG City (B051/C050).
Hall 8.1: MBC Game Studio (A011/B010), The District (B060), GIGABYTE/AORUS (C050) and Mattel (B020).
Hall 9.1: JBL Quantum (B034/C035) and Rocket Beans TV (A046/B047).

New: The District, gamescom's first competitive-gaming area — the back of Hall 8.1 plus outdoor space in P8, headlined by SK Gaming, with CLUTCH, Star Wars Galactic Racer and a Red Bull EA Sports FC 27 tournament.
New: 4Divinity brings six titles across Halls 6.1, 7.1 and 4.2 — The Defiant, Showa American Story, Guns of Eschaton, A Whisper of Fall: Jinyiwei, Genigods: Nezha and Sword Sage: Awakening.
New area on the Info tab: Outdoor Area P8 behind Hall 8 — gamescom Beach, Asian Garden, Community Wall, CD Projekt Red's Apollo Tent and the outdoor half of The District.
The small unnamed counters in Halls 6.1, 7.1, 8.1 and 9.1 are the official gamescom merchandise shops. They have a card now, and the map names them.

Aerosoft's five “unannounced simulators” have names: Notruf 112 – Die Feuerwehr, Firefighters Code Red, Notaufnahme Simulator, Heavy Cargo: The Truck Simulator, Bergwerk: A Mining Sim, Forensics: Crime Scene Detective and Seaworks: Trap Season.
Tencent's Hall 8.1 stand has a programme after all: Honor of Kings and Arena of Valor, with cosplayers and competitions.
Added Seafarer: The Ship Sim and Worms W.M.D. to the Team17 × astragon booth, and Final Fantasy VII Remake to Square Enix.
Fixed: ASUS also holds B040 next to its main Hall 8.1 stand — the map was calling that booth uncovered.
Fixed a dead link: the Indie Arena Booth's site is indiearenabooth.de. Every other outbound link was re-checked and resolves.
Fixed on the map: booths with an upper floor were drawn twice, and the empty upper copy caught the tap. 69 phantom stands across eleven halls are gone, and every affected booth is tappable again.
Electronic Arts' Hall 6.1 stand is confirmed: booth B011/A010, next to the hall entrance. The lineup is still unannounced beyond EA Sports FC 27.
New exhibitor: Daedalic Entertainment, Hall 10.2 booth E020/D021 — six adventure titles, including Woodo, Ghost Haunting and Star Trek: Voyager — Across the Unknown.
Fixed HoYoverse's Hall 6.1 stand: it is the two-part booth B030/C031, not just B030.
Eclipse Glow Games' Hall 6.1 stand (B050) is now confirmed in the official directory, as is Focus Entertainment's shared stand with Team17/astragon at B060/C061.
Saturday (Aug 29) day tickets are sold out — only the evening ticket from 16:00 remains. Ticket and crowd guidance updated.
Opening Night Live gains a reveal: a gameplay trailer for Game of Thrones: War for Westeros. Stream only, no show-floor booth.
Re-confirmed: Wargaming and Take-Two/2K have no show-floor booth this year, and Kuro Games still has no confirmed attendance.
Directory refresh: still 1,658 registered exhibitors, no new registrations.
The guide now speaks German. It follows your browser on the first visit, and a switcher in the header and footer changes it whenever you like.
Everything a visitor reads is translated: booth descriptions, queue calls, visit advice, the planner, the hall map and the calendar export.
Game titles, exhibitor names and area names stay in their own language, so every share link keeps working — a list built in German opens in English and back.
Your phone only downloads the language you read, and both are cached, so switching still works in a hall with no reception.
The imprint, the privacy page and this changelog stay in English. The guide says so under the Updates heading when you read in German.

New Entrances section on the Info tab, covering all four gates: South is where the rail crowd lands and the business halls sit, North is shortest to halls 6–9, East opens into Hall 10, West is the quiet one.
Trade-badge access is now stated where it matters: the entertainment halls open at 09:00 every day, an hour before the public on Thursday and Friday.
“West is best” now says when it is true — Thursday and Friday, when South and East carry the public. Halls 2–4 sit at the South entrance.
Accredited creators are named alongside trade visitors and press as having business-area access.

New: trade exhibitors. Turn on "I have a trade badge" and the ~820 business-hall booths become saveable, plannable stops — with their own list, product-group filters, curated cards and map coverage. Off by default; a consumer ticket does not open halls 2–4.

The switch is a Badge row at the top of the filters — Consumer or Trade & media — and it is repeated under "Your badge" in Event info. Same control both ways round, so turning it off is as quick as turning it on.

The hall map carries the switch too, in the purple business-area banner, and in the stand details when you tap a business booth the guide is not yet showing you. Fix: business-hall booths no longer stay on the map after trade exhibitors are switched back off.

52 curated business-area cards. The B2B names first, because they were missing from the guide entirely: Cloudflare, AWS, servers.com, G-Core, Unity, CurseForge & Overwolf, Xsolla, Keywords, Sumo Digital, Virtuos, Denuvo, Sensor Tower, IGN & Humble Bundle, Fandom, Reddit, Opera, Owlchemy, Poki, Blacknut, Kakao Games, NVIDIA, the IGDA and Women in Games International.
Plus the national pavilions (Spain/ICEX, GamingMalta, Denmark/NIMBI, the UK collective, the Nordic & Baltic stand, Games Hubs Hessen).

Exhibitors with a booth on both sides of the show — Capcom, Ubisoft, Xbox, Nintendo, Bandai Namco, CD Projekt, KRAFTON, Atari, HoYoverse, Focus, GIANTS, Razer, Corsair, Samsung, Raw Fury, Coffee Stain, Bloober, SCS, Wargaming and more — now have one card you can turn over. Tap the small purple square in the corner of the hall plate and the card switches to its business booth; tap the orange one to switch back.
Purple means business area throughout, taken from the official hall plan's own colour for those halls — the same one the map washes them with.

The two booths stay separate stops in your plan, because they keep different hours: the business area shuts after Friday while the consumer halls run all weekend. Assign a business-hall stop to Saturday or Sunday and the planner warns you — on the row, in the day header, and in the calendar export.
Every trade booth says whether you can walk up or need an appointment. Almost all of them are walk-up; only about twenty of the 821 are closed meeting compounds.
Exhibitor rows now carry the official product-group tags (Development, Service firms, eSports…), filterable in the trade list.
Hall map: the business halls fill in. Hall 2.1 went from almost no coverage to 60 of its 78 stands named, and tapping one shows the exhibitor, its country and its product groups.
Fix: hall 1 is the public Event Arena, not the business area — its one directory booth is no longer labelled trade-only.

The business halls are on the map. Halls 2.1, 2.2, 3.2, 4.1 and 4.2 are drawn booth by booth like the rest, which is 366 more stands and most of the Full directory — so a row in hall 3.2 now opens on its stand instead of stopping at plain text. They open under a banner saying what they are: trade and media badge only, and closed after Friday. A consumer ticket still does not open that door; the map just stops pretending the hall isn't there.

Halls are colour-coded by area, in the same colours the official plan uses: cyan for the entertainment halls your ticket opens, purple for the trade-only business ones. The hall row groups them under those colours and the hall's own structure is washed in it, so it takes no reading to tell which kind of hall you are in. Saved booths are still orange over everything.
Booth outlines were re-checked against Koelnmesse's data while adding them: the retro block at A-020 in hall 10.2 now names the exhibitors on both its levels, five of which were missing.

Share list now asks who the link is for. Someone else gets your saved list alone — your progress through it is not theirs. Another of my devices brings your day plan and played marks along too, and on arrival offers to replace that device's list instead of adding to it, so removing a booth or moving it to another day finally carries across your own devices. The prompt counts what a replace would remove before anything is touched, and Undo puts all of it back.

Shared links are much shorter, which brings the QR code back: a 30-stop list had quietly outgrown it as the guide's data doubled, and now fits again with its whole day plan riding along. Links shared before this change keep working.

Booth numbers for four booths that had none: SEGA / Atlus (Hall 7.1, A031 and A041/B040), Square Enix (8.1 A021), Plaion (9.1 B030/C031) and Embark Studios (6.1 B041/A040 and B051/A050). All four were on Koelnmesse's own hall plan the whole time.

Exhibitors with more than one stand now list all of them. Ubisoft has a second, smaller booth across the aisle in Hall 6.1 (B020); Nintendo holds four stands in 9.1, LEGO three, and Headis, Gryphline and KRAFTON two each. Tapping any of them on the map now names the exhibitor instead of saying the stand is not covered.

Fixed: tapping a booth with an upper floor reported "no exhibitor filed for this stand" — the Indie Arena Booth, Razer, Bilibili, Tencent, Gryphline, Infold, PXN, 8BitDo and Eclipse Glow Games, plus 25 booths the guide has no card for. Koelnmesse files the gallery as a second stand on the same outline, and that empty upper one was catching every tap. The two are now one booth, and its sheet names both stand numbers.

Every booth number in the Full directory now opens the hall map on that exact stand — so a studio with no card of its own is one tap from knowing where it stands, not just which hall it is in. Booths in the business halls stay plain text; a consumer ticket does not open those doors.

The halls and booth numbers named in Your plan, Queue priority and the 18+ wristband list are links to the map too. Tapping "Hall 9.1" on a stop takes you to that booth, not just that hall — and a game shown at two booths links to both. In the by-hall walking order, the header still opens the whole hall and each stop's booth number opens its stand.

New: a Hall map. Every hall you can visit is drawn booth by booth, with names on the booths instead of the blank white boxes the official plan gives you — and your saved booths lit up in orange so you can see your day laid out in the hall.
Tap the hall plate on any exhibitor card to jump straight to that booth on the map; tap a booth on the map to see its lineup, queue forecast and save it. Saving works the same in both directions.
The map works offline like the rest of the guide — all seven halls are stored on your device, which is the point when reception dies inside Koelnmesse.
Booth outlines come from Koelnmesse's official hall-plan data, credited and dated at the foot of the map.

22 new booths from a full sweep of Hall 10 — the half of the show that never makes the news. MOZA Racing runs six sim-racing and flight rigs at 10.1 A022 and takes free bookings online before the show, which is the difference between sitting down and watching.

New category, Experiences & Activities, for booths where the draw is something you do rather than a game you demo: MOZA's rigs, Kawasaki's rideable CORLEO robot at 10.1 D010, XelerateVR, an RC drift track and Headis in 10.2, and the gamescom LAN area.

Hall 10.1's retro corner is now covered properly: the revived Commodore (C059/B050, showing the C64 Ultimate), MicroProse (A060/B061) and Embracer Freemode at F061, whose RedOctane team is behind the new Guitar Hero-style Stage Tour.

Hardware row added: Corsair, PNY, Thermaltake, ASRock, PXN's wheels, 8BitDo in 10.2, and the genuinely strange hi-fi corner at A070 where konsolenfan.de hosts Yamaha, Genelec, ELAC and Canton. Logitech G's second stand now carries its booth number (10.1 E074/F077).

Also new: Raw Fury, RocketWerkz, Frozen District, AREA 35, and A MAZE.'s experimental-games PlayGround in 10.2. A gamescom Campus entry explains that about half of Hall 10.1 is recruiting and education, not demos.

New Full directory section under the exhibitor grid: all 1,630 booths registered with gamescom, searchable by name, hall and booth number. Indie Arena Booth and other shared stands name the booth their studios sit on, so a studio you can't find in the guide is still findable on the floor. It only downloads when you open it.
New: every exhibitor card now shows where its information came from — the ⓘ marker next to the official-page link opens the list of sources behind that booth's location, lineup and queue call.
Each list says when the entry was last checked, so a booth still marked "unconf." can be verified at the source before you plan a day around it.
The Event info tab carries the same marker for the dates, hours, ticket prices and hall areas on that page.
The planner's itinerary and Route by hall are now one section — Your plan: the same saved stops, arranged by day or by hall with one tap instead of two near-identical lists stacked on the page.
The hall view now reads your day assignments: every stop shows which day it's planned for, and once anything is placed, day chips filter the route to a single day — your Thursday, in walking order.
A saved game keeps listing every booth running it in the single-day route, so "pick the shorter queue" works inside a day plan too.
Nothing about your data moved: saved list, day assignments and played marks are untouched, and the arrangement you pick is remembered on this device like the other view preferences.
New: assign each saved booth or game to a specific gamescom day, with unassigned picks kept together until you're ready to place them.
Each itinerary day shows its opening hours, access rules and crowd advice inline, so the plan stays useful while you move through the halls.
Export the assigned day plan as a calendar (.ics) file, with each day's stops collected into one event.
Stops you've marked played dim and sink to the bottom of their itinerary day, so each group leads with what's still left to do.
Your itinerary stays in this browser only, alongside your saved list — day assignments are not part of shared links, and nothing is sent anywhere.
Focus Entertainment's Hall 6.1 booth (B060/C061) is confirmed on Focus' own gamescom exhibitor profile, not just third-party trackers — no need to double-check it before you go.

Grinding Gear Games' Path of Exile 2 booth (Hall 6.1, B031) is likewise confirmed on GGG's own gamescom profile; GGG also streams a new content reveal on gamescom's official Twitch channel Aug 25, 20:00 CEST, ahead of the show-floor demo.
New: Route by hall on the Visit planner groups your saved stops in hall-number order, with offsite and unannounced locations — plus absent exhibitors — called out separately.
Route stops carry the played tick too: a played stop dims, drops to the end of its hall, and respects the Hide played toggle.
Booth cards now link to the exhibitor's official gamescom page, where the exhibitor publishes its own booth program, stage times and trailers — 46 of the 53 booths have one.

No link on CD Projekt Red, Take-Two/Rockstar, THQ Nordic, Wargaming and Kuro Games (not registered as exhibitors), on AMD (co-registered on the shared Hall 7.1 community stand rather than under its own name), or on Samsung (gamescom has switched its profile page off).

Trade Wednesday reality-check added: a trade badge doesn't open every booth on Aug 26 — some big exhibitors reserve the morning (or the whole day) for invited press. Notes added to the day planner, crowd tips and affected exhibitor entries.

Xbox booth hours corrected per Xbox Wire: Thu/Fri 10:00–20:00, Sat/Sun 9:00–20:00 — the booth is closed on trade Wednesday apart from the evening FanFest (its Wednesday has traditionally been an invited-press preview).
Capcom: in 2025 the booth admitted only press until ~11:00 on Wednesday — trade visitors should plan Wednesday visits for late morning onwards.
Fifteen exhibitors added after a full sweep of the official 1,610-entry exhibitor directory and follow-up research — press coverage had surfaced almost none of them.
New: Aternos (Hall 10.1, B030/C031) — the free Minecraft server host runs 'MC Party' with the Cytooxien team: four custom minigames, with coins to spend on merch and MGA Miniverse collectibles.
New: Infold Games (Hall 9.1, A054/B055) — Infinity Nikki meet-and-greets, activities and exclusive merch; Love and Deepspace expected back too.
New: Gryphline's Arknights: Endfield returns bigger, with two Hall 8.1 stand blocks and Boss Speedrun Challenges.
New: GIANTS Software (Farming Simulator) at Hall 6.1, B061; SCS Software's Euro/American Truck Simulator rigs at Hall 10.1, B022/C023.
New: Behaviour Interactive (Dead by Daylight's 10th-anniversary year) at Hall 10.1, E072; Bloober Team at C040/D041.
New: Kepler Interactive shows ONTOS — Frictional Games' SOMA successor — at Hall 10.1, B093.
New: Magic: The Gathering (Wizards of the Coast) anchors the Hall 5.2 card corner; Atari heads a retro cluster with the revived Commodore and MicroProse in Hall 10.1.
New: Snail Games (Hall 8.1, A041) — ARK: Survival Ascended content, For The Stars, Bellwright and Honeycomb, plus a first look at an unannounced AAA title.
New: Aerosoft (Hall 9.1, B043) — Winter Resort 3, Professional Ship Simulator and five first-time sim reveals (police work, mining, firefighting, crab fishing, roadmaking).
New: Coffee Stain (Satisfactory; publisher of Valheim and Deep Rock Galactic) at Hall 10.1, A062/B063; Koei Tecmo with a small Hall 10.2 stand.
New: AMD co-anchors the shared Hall 7.1 community block (B041/C040) with Ryzen/Radeon rigs — and teases a Radeon announcement at its own Cologne event on Aug 23.

Now officially confirmed in the directory: Focus (6.1 B060/C061, sharing the stand block with Team17 × astragon), KRAFTON's two stand blocks (9.1 B050/C051 + B040/C041) and Urban Games' Transport Fever 3 stand (8.1 B053a).
Corrected: Pearl Abyss is at 9.1 B010/C011 and Samsung's own Odyssey stand at B020/C029 — the two were swapped. Samsung stays co-registered at the Pearl Abyss stand it powers.
Tencent is officially on the show floor too: Hall 8.1, B050/A051 (program unannounced) — separate from the offsite Worlds of Play art exhibition.
Hall labels now match the official directory (6.1/7.1/8.1/9.1), so the hall filter no longer splits the same hall in two.

NetEase's Hall 7.1 booths are now officially confirmed: A051 for Sea of Remnants, B050 for Marvel Rivals (Season 9.5) and Where Winds Meet — plus a trade-only Business Area preview of Once Human's next expansion (Hall 4.2, D050).

Tick ✓ on a game once you've played it — the row dims, and the same title is marked at every booth showing it.
A booth counts as played when you tick it directly or finish every game you saved there; save another game and it becomes active again.
Played booths sink below the rest of the queue-priority list without losing their original rank, and the new 'Hide played' switch removes them altogether.
Your played history and hide preference live in this browser only, work offline and never leave your device.
New: hide 18+ demos or show only age-gated booths, with badges distinguishing confirmed wristband checks from expected restrictions.
The Visit planner now groups booths with adult demos into a wristband checklist, so you can collect the red band before queueing.
New: share your saved booths and games as a link, with a scannable QR code for moving a plan from desktop to phone.
Opening a shared link never replaces your list: an empty list loads immediately with Undo, while an existing list asks before adding only the new items.
Shared links are built entirely in the browser and contain guide identifiers only — exhibitor IDs and compact game codes — so nothing is uploaded or sent anywhere unless you share the link yourself.
Link sharing and QR generation work offline; the QR encoder is dependency-free and included in the app cache.

Wednesday's discounted Wildcard ticket has sold out — Thursday is now the best low-crowd public day for hands-on demos.
New: save the booths and games you actually care about with the + button, then tick 'Saved' to filter the exhibitor list down to just those.

The queue-priority list on the Visit planner filters the same way, and counts a publisher as saved when you've saved any game they're showing — save Fable and Xbox stays in your list, with the matching titles named on the row.
Saving a game saves it at every booth showing it, so you can compare queues for the titles that appear twice (Alien: Isolation 2, Modern Warfare 4 and six others).
